question_text: In a class there are 30 students. If each student plays a chess game with each of the other students, then find the total number of chess games played by them.

recall_prompt: Say how you would count the chess games among thirty students — why a game is a selection of two, and the number.
insider_note: One game is one pair of students, so the count is ³⁰C₂ = 435. Any working that reaches 870 has counted each game twice, once from each player’s side.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: One game = one pair of students
steps.margin_note: First mark. A game needs 2 of the 30 students, and A playing B is the same game as B playing A — order does not matter: ³⁰C₂.
lines: One game needs 2 of the 30 students;
A with B is the same game as B with A,
so order does not matter: ³⁰C₂

recall.must_convey: That each game is an unordered pair of students, so the count is 30 C 2.
accept: each game is a pair of students and order does not matter so it is thirty C two
choose two students out of thirty for a game, a combination
oka game ki iddaru students, order lekunda, thirty C two
A with B and B with A is the same game so combination

steps.why: The question is really asking how many pairs of students there are. Using ³⁰P₂ would count each game twice, once from each player's side.

steps.label: Evaluate ³⁰C₂

accept: thirty into twenty nine by two is four hundred thirty five
fifteen times twenty nine is four hundred and thirty five
thirty C two four thirty five
the answer is four hundred thirty five games

steps.why: Halving 30 × 29 removes the double count; 15 × 29 is the easy way to do the arithmetic.
